item.title: D4vd Must Stand Trial in Celeste Rivas Hernandez Murder Case, Judge Rules
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we bring you the latest updates on high-profile cases. Today, we're discussing the shocking allegations against singer D4vd, also known as David Anthony Burke. A judge has decided that prosecutors have enough evidence to take him to trial for the alleged murder of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Let's dive into the details."
[Short music transition]
Host: "According to Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman, Judge Charlaine F. Olmedo ruled on Monday that prosecutors have met their burden of showing 'probable cause' for the charges against D4vd. This means the case can move forward toward trial. The prosecution alleges that D4vd stabbed and dismembered Rivas in April 2025, after she threatened to reveal their illegal sexual relationship, which could have derailed his music career."
[Short music transition]
Host: "The preliminary hearing, which lasted five days, presented gruesome evidence, including photos of Rivas' partially decomposed body parts, testimony from a medical examiner, and text messages between Rivas and D4vd. The texts revealed that Rivas had an abortion at the age of 13. An executive from Interscope also testified that D4vd made millions of dollars from his music, supporting the prosecution's theory that he stood to lose a lucrative career if Rivas came forward."
[Short music transition]
Host: "D4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges, including first-degree murder, child sexual abuse, and mutilating a body. His attorneys have stated that they will 'vigorously defend' him in court, claiming that the actual evidence will show that D4vd did not murder Rivas. A trial date has not been set, but D4vd is expected to appear in court again at the end of August. The District Attorney's Office is still considering whether to seek the death penalty against him."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's update on the D4vd case. We'll continue to follow this story and bring you updates as more information becomes available. Thanks for tuning in."
